There are a smooth even function B : T → [0, Kδ] and, for every positive integer N, real numbers YN,k ∈ [−1, 1] (0 ≤ k < N) and a smooth function BN : T → C such that BN (−t) = BN (t), |BN (t)| = B(t), ∥UYN − BN ∥∞ = Oδ(N−1 ), (28) Z T B(t)2 dt ≥ 1 − 7δ, 1 N N−1 X k=0 Y 2 N,k ≥ 1 − 8δ for all sufficiently large N. (29) The function B vanishes near 0 and 1/2. Its superlevel set {t ∈ [0, 1/2] : B(t) ≥ b} is a nonempty finite union of pairwise disjoint closed intervals of positive length, contained in (0, 1/2). Let Jj = [uj, vj], 1 ≤ j ≤ M, be the closures of its complementary intervals in [0, 1/2], and put lj = vj − uj > 0, L = M X j=1 lj, 0 < L ≤ C0δ, C0 = 10. (30) 13 Thus B ≤ b on the gaps Jj and B ≥ b off their union. An endpoint z of a gap other than 0 and 1/2 is called a transition endpoint. At each such z, B(z) = b, and on a neighborhood Vz ⊂ (0, 1/2) there are a real constant αz and a real quadratic polynomial ψz such that, for every N, BN (t) = B(t)e αz + Nψz(t)  (t ∈ Vz), xz := ψ′ z(z) ∈ (0, 1).
